author: Karl Rock
description:
Long before social media or business cards, skilled stone masons found another way to advertise - their own work.

At the Chaukhandi Tombs in Sindh, Pakistan, some of the craftsmen carved their names directly onto the tombs they created. It was a way to showcase their skill and reputation, helping future customers know exactly who had produced the intricate carvings.

These centuries-old signatures offer a fascinating glimpse into the lives of the artisans behind one of Pakistan's most remarkable historical sites.
title: The Oldest Form of Marketing?

author: Karl Rock
description:
Walking through the Chaukhandi Tombs in Sindh, Pakistan, I couldn't help but wonder - why don't we build tombs like this anymore?

These beautifully carved sandstone monuments date from the 15th to 18th centuries and were created as lasting memorials for tribal leaders, warriors, and their families. Every carving tells a story, from traditional jewellery and textiles to horses, weapons, and intricate geometric designs.

They're a reminder that history wasn't only written in books - it was carved into stone.
title: Would You Want a Tomb Like This?
